description: Cerium is a soft, ductile, and silvery-white metal that is the second element in the lanthanide series with atomic number 58. It tarnishes when exposed to air and is considered one of the rare-earth elements. Cerium often shows an oxidation state of +3 characteristic of the lanthanide series, but also has a stable +4 state that does not oxidize water.
uses: Cerium(IV) oxide is used to polish glass and is an important part of catalytic converters. Cerium metal is used in ferrocerium lighters for its pyrophoric properties. Cerium-doped YAG phosphor is used in conjunction with blue light-emitting diodes to produce white light in most commercial white LED light sources.
characteristics: Cerium is a ductile metal with a hardness similar to that of silver, and its estimated abundance in the Earth's crust is 68 ppm. It is highly electropositive and reacts with water, and metallic cerium can be highly pyrophoric. Cerium has a variable electronic structure and exhibits four allotropic forms at standard pressure with different crystal structures depending on temperature.
